snp2.2:1.2:
millet, Job’s tears, green gram,
leaf-fruit, tuber-fruit, water-chestnut-fruit,
snp2.2:1.3: obtained in line with the Dhamma,
snp2.2:1.4:
don’t desire sensual-pleasures
or tell falsehoods.
snp2.2:2.1: But when eating what is well-made,
snp2.2:2.2:
well-prepared,
exquisite, given, offered by others,
snp2.2:2.4: Kassapa, one consumes a raw stench.
snp2.2:3.1: Yet you, kinsman of Brahmā, say,
snp2.2:3.2: ‘Raw stench is not proper for me,’
snp2.2:3.4: and the well-prepared fleshes of birds.
snp2.2:3.5: So I ask you, Kassapa, the meaning of that:
snp2.2:3.6: Of what sort is ‘raw stench’ for you?”
snp2.2:4.1:
The Buddha Kassapa:
“Killing living beings,
hunting, cutting, binding,
snp2.2:4.3:
useless recitations,
associating with the wives of others:
snp2.2:4.4:
This is a raw stench,
not the eating of meat.
snp2.2:5.1:
Those people here
who are unrestrained in sensuality,
snp2.2:5.2:
greedy for flavors,
mixed together with what’s impure,
snp2.2:5.4:
This is a raw stench,
not the eating of meat.
snp2.2:6.1:
Those who are rough, pitiless,
eating the flesh off your back,
snp2.2:6.3:
habitually ungenerous,
giving to no one:
snp2.2:6.4:
This is a raw stench,
not the eating of meat.
snp2.2:7.3:
conceit & pride,
befriending those of no integrity:
snp2.2:7.4:
This is a raw stench,
not the eating of meat.
snp2.2:8.1:
Those of evil habits,
debt-repudiators, informers,
snp2.2:8.3: vile men who do evil things:
snp2.2:8.4:
This is a raw stench,
not the eating of meat.
snp2.2:9.1:
Those people here
who are unrestrained toward beings,
snp2.2:9.2:
taking what’s others’,
intent on injury,
snp2.2:9.4:
This is a raw stench,
not the eating of meat.
snp2.2:10.2:
constantly intent
on hindering and killing;
beings who, after passing away,
go to darkness,
snp2.2:10.4:
This is a raw stench,
not the eating of meat.
snp2.2:11.2:
no nakedness,
no shaven head, no tangled hair,
snp2.2:11.3:
no rough animal skins,
no performance of fire oblations,
snp2.2:11.4:
or the many austerities
to become an immortal in the world,
snp2.2:11.5:
no chants, no oblations,
no performance of sacrifices
at the proper season—
snp2.2:11.6:
purify a mortal
who hasn’t crossed over doubt.
snp2.2:12.1:
One should go about
guarded
with regard to those things,
one’s faculties understood,
snp2.2:12.2:
standing firm in the Dhamma,
delighting in being straightforward
& mild.
snp2.2:12.3:
Attachments past,
all suffering abandoned,
the enlightened one
snp2.2:12.4:
isn’t smeared
by what’s heard or seen.”
snp2.2:13.1:
Thus the Blessed One,
explained the meaning again & again.
snp2.2:13.2:
The one
who had mastered chants
understood it.
snp2.2:13.4:
the sage—
free from raw stench,
unfettered, indomitable—
proclaimed it.
snp2.2:14.1:
Hearing the Awakened One’s
well-spoken word—
snp2.2:14.2:
free from raw stench,
dispelling all stress—
snp2.2:14.3:
the one with lowered mind
paid homage to the Tathāgata,
snp2.2:14.4: chose the Going Forth right there.
